title: OneDrive: guided rename and move flow for max path sync errors on Windows
summary: The briefing passes: the planned Windows error experience and January rollout window match Microsoft's roadmap and tenant notice. The existing folder-name control and product licensing are documented, and searches found no separate switch or feature-specific price.

claims.claim: SharePoint limits documents a 400-character decoded file-path limit for OneDrive and SharePoint in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The entire decoded file path, including the file name, can't contain more than 400 characters for OneDrive, OneDrive for work or school and SharePoint in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Microsoft Support describes the 520-character sync path as a local path of up to 400 characters plus the OneDrive root folder.
claims.quote: The total path is the combination of the local path (up to 400 characters) and the OneDrive root folder (up to 120 characters). Paths exceeding 520 characters show a sync error.

claims.claim: The full OneDrive sync root folder path cannot exceed 120 characters.
claims.quote: The full OneDrive sync root folder path (for example, `C:\Users\{alias}\OneDrive - {organization name}`) cannot exceed 120 characters.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Group Policy Management Editor exposes the folder-name control at Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > OneDrive > Set a custom name for the OneDrive folder.
claims.quote:
Under Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\OneDrive
Computer Configuration policies in the Group Policy Management Editor
### Set a custom name for the OneDrive folder

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The documented registry setting is [HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive\CustomSyncRootFolderName] "TenantID"="CustomFolderName".
claims.quote:
Enabling this policy sets the following registry key to the value shown in the following example:
`[HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive\CustomSyncRootFolderName] "TenantID"="CustomFolderName"`

claims.claim: The custom folder-name setting shortens the local sync root name and increases available path length for nested folders and files.
claims.quote: This setting lets you customize the local OneDrive sync root folder name on users' computers. By default, the folder name is *OneDrive - {organization name}*. Shortening this name increases the available path length for nested folders and files.

claims.claim: The enabled custom folder-name policy applies when creating the sync root folder for new users.
claims.quote: If you enable this setting and provide a custom folder name, OneDrive will use that name when creating the sync root folder for new users.

claims.claim: Existing syncing users must unlink and relink their account for the custom folder name to take effect.
claims.quote: Users who are already syncing will need to unlink and relink their account for the change to take effect.

claims.claim: The custom folder-name policy is documented for Group Policy, not Intune.
claims.quote:
### Set a custom name for the OneDrive folder

*Applies to: Group Policy*

claims.claim: The custom folder-name policy is an existing path-length control, not a control over the new rename and move experience.
claims.quote: This setting lets you customize the local OneDrive sync root folder name on users' computers.
